title: Cerebellar volume predicted effector genes (Chambers T et al. 2022)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Genetic common variants associated with cerebellar volume and their overlap with mental disorders: a study on 33,265 individuals from the UK-Biobank.
Chambers T, et al.
Mol Psychiatry. 2022 Apr;27(4):2282-2290. doi: 10.1038/s41380-022-01443-8.
PMID: 35079123

The authors performed a GWAS of total cerebellar volume and underlying cerebellar lobe volumes in 33,265 individuals from the UK Biobank cohort. At the GWAS significant loci, they assessed whether the index SNP or its proxies caused coding changes in a nearby gene, affected expression levels of a gene in cerebellar tissue, or were associated with cerebellar expression of a gene based on summary data-based Mendelian randomization. The table below lists potential effector genes at the loci with the strongest supporting evidence. Mouse over the column headers for more details about each evidence type.
